---
title: "Model workspace and data"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_arrow <- requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(multimod)
```

A model's data can be large. multimod keeps the model structure and the
data apart on disk: `save_model()` writes a *workspace*, a directory with
the R object for the structure and one data file per set, mapping and
parameter, in CSV, Arrow IPC or Parquet. `load_model()` reads it back, with
or without the data, and `get_data()` fetches a table from disk on demand.
The generated JuMP and Pyomo code reads the same files at run time, which
is why `write_jump()` and `write_pyomo()` create a workspace when they are
given an empty `model_dir`.

## Layout

```
<model_dir>/
  model.rds              the model structure, as saved
  metadata.json          counts and format, for readers outside R
  format.txt             "csv", "ipc" or "parquet"
  sets/<name>/data.*     one file per set, column `member`
  mappings/<name>/data.* one file per mapping, one column per dimension
  parameters/<name>/data.*          dimension columns plus `value`
  parameters/<name>/folded_data/data.*   if the parameter is folded
  variables/<name>/data.*           solution values, after a solve
  solution_log.txt       one line per solution load
  solvers/<backend>/     generated code and the backend's output
```

## Save and load

```{r save}
toy <- example_models$toy
ws <- tempfile("toy-")
toy <- save_model(toy, ws, format = "csv", verbose = FALSE)
list.files(ws, recursive = TRUE)[1:8]
toy$base_path == ws
```

`save_model()` returns the model with `base_path` set to the workspace.
With `format = "ipc"` or `"parquet"` the data files are Arrow files, smaller
and faster to read; both need the 'arrow' package, and the generated Julia
and Python read them as readily as CSV.

```{r save-ipc, eval = has_arrow}
ws_ipc <- tempfile("toy-ipc-")
save_model(toy, ws_ipc, format = "ipc", verbose = FALSE)
list.files(file.path(ws_ipc, "parameters"), recursive = TRUE)
```

`load_model()` reads the structure and, by default, every data table:

```{r load}
m <- load_model(ws, verbose = FALSE)
head(m$parameters$pAvail$data)
```

## Data on demand

A large model is loaded without its data and asked for one table at a time.
`get_data()` reads the table from the workspace and caches it in the model
object it returns from.

```{r lazy}
m <- load_model(ws, load_data = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
is.null(m$parameters$pAvail$data)
get_data(m, "pAvail", type = "parameter")
get_data(m, "mTR", type = "mapping")
get_data(m, "tech", type = "set")
```

## Changing data

`update_parameter()` replaces a parameter's table; with `auto_save = TRUE`
the file in the workspace is rewritten at the same time.

```{r update}
d <- get_data(m, "pDemand", type = "parameter")
d$value <- d$value * 1.1
m <- update_parameter(m, "pDemand", d, auto_save = TRUE)
read.csv(file.path(ws, "parameters", "pDemand", "data.csv"))
```

The structure is unchanged, so the model can be re-solved on the new data
through any route, for example in R:

```{r resolve, eval = requireNamespace("highs", quietly = TRUE)}
m <- load_model(ws, verbose = FALSE)
solve_highs(m, attach = FALSE)$objective
```

## Solutions

The file routes write their results under `solvers/<backend>/solution/`.
With `load_results = TRUE` (the default when a model is passed),
`solve_gmpl()`, `solve_jump()` and `solve_pyomo()` read the variable values
into `model$variables[[name]]$solution`, copy them to `variables/`, and
append a line to `solution_log.txt`, so the workspace always holds the
latest solution and a record of when it was loaded.

```{r solutions, eval = FALSE}
r <- solve_jump(m, ws)
r$model$variables$vGen$solution
r$model$solution_metadata$variables_loaded
readLines(file.path(ws, "solution_log.txt"))
```

## Folded data

A folded parameter (see `vignette("folding")`) keeps both tables: the
original under `data.*` and the reduced one under `folded_data/data.*`.
`save_model()` writes both, `load_model()` reads both, and the writers take
the folded table when the model is folded.

## Reading the files elsewhere

The data files are plain CSV or Arrow and need nothing from multimod:

```python
import pyarrow.feather as feather
demand = feather.read_feather("ws/parameters/pDemand/data.arrow")
```

```julia
using Arrow, DataFrames
demand = DataFrame(Arrow.Table("ws/parameters/pDemand/data.arrow"))
```

`metadata.json` lists the counts and the format so a reader can orient
itself without R.

```{r metadata}
cat(readLines(file.path(ws, "metadata.json")), sep = "\n")
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(c(ws, if (exists("ws_ipc")) ws_ipc), recursive = TRUE)
```
